strokes.text: This guide takes an empty scene collection to one scene with a coloured background and a filter.
Along the way it shows the plan, apply and verify loop that the provider is built around.
Before You Start
Install OBS Studio and enable the WebSocket server under Tools, WebSocket Server Settings.
Leave the base canvas at 1920x1080 under Settings, Video, which is the size this guide assumes.
Create a scene collection for this guide, here called My Show, and leave it selected.
Stop streaming, recording, the virtual camera and the replay buffer, because the provider refuses to write while any output is active.
Use a scene collection made for Terraform: `obs_scene_contents` removes every placement it does not list.
Configuration
Save this as `main.tf` in an empty directory:
ex:guides/getting-started
The `collection` local names the scene collection, and every resource repeats it.
@resources/source creates the source together with its first placement, the anchor, in the scene.
@resources/filter attaches to the source through `parent_uuid`, so Terraform creates the source first.
@resources/scene_contents lists every placement the scene holds, bottom layer first.
Apply
terraform init
terraform plan -out=show.tfplan
terraform apply show.tfplan
OBS shows the new scene as soon as the apply finishes.
Run `terraform plan` again: it reports no changes, which confirms that what OBS holds is what the configuration declares.
Change Something
Edit a field of `anchor_transform`, for example `x`, then plan and apply.
The plan shows one placement changing in place, and the source keeps its UUID.
Now drag the source somewhere else in OBS and plan again: the provider reports the drift, and the next apply puts the placement back.
Next Steps
@guides/ownership-and-ordering explains anchors, extra placements and layer order.
@guides/importing brings scenes and sources that already exist under management.
@guides/verified-writes describes what the provider checks around every write.
